newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rail privatisation bid to be in by Nov 30.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rail privatisation bid to be in by Nov 30.

text.p: A consortium led by conglomerate Renong Bhd has until November 30 to submit its proposal for the privatisation of Malaysia's railway network, Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik said on Monday.
"The consortium has been given a letter of exclusivity to submit their proposal to the Economic Planning Unit before November 30," he was quoted by the national Bernama news agency as saying.
Other members of the consortium are Diversified Resources Bhd (DRB) and Bolton Properties Bhd.
Renong will take up a 50 percent stake in Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) while DRB and Bolton will take up 30 percent and 20 percent respectively.
Ling said it was a "very strong" consortium that would bring a lot of benefits to KTMB which was corporatised in August 1992.
He added the government had decided that there would be no more privatisation of KTMB's landbank except for projects which were on-going or contractually committed.
KTMB is reported to have a 12,656-hectare landbank valued at more than one billion ringgit.
